notes: מַחְסוֹם is the direct object of the second אֶשְׁמְרָה and the ASV keeps that verb as an English verb with a different object ('keep my mouth'), demoting the Hebrew object to an instrument. Rule 33's direct-object paragraph and its PRO.7.16 precedent ('I have spread my couch with carpets') give the supplied 'with' to the verb's unit under rule 44, not to the noun. The verb's unit becomes discontinuous around 'my mouth' and 'a' under rule 25; the noun keeps 'a bridle' with its supplied article under rule 15.
